title: Sleep–glucose coupling: a review
summary: Short sleep duration (6h vs 8h) is associated with a 20–40% higher postprandial glucose excursion and impaired insulin sensitivity the next morning. Consistent early-morning light exposure improves this coupling within 14 days.

title: 14-day morning-walk + light-eating protocol
summary: A structured 14-day trial combining a 20-minute morning walk before the first meal and reducing evening calories by 25% produces measurable improvements in fasting glucose and self-reported afternoon energy. Effect size: moderate (SMD ≈ 0.4).

title: Sleep and stress interaction
summary: Chronic psychological stress suppresses slow-wave sleep and delays REM onset. HRV (high-frequency) drops 10–20% over 2–4 weeks of sustained stress before any subjective fatigue is noticed.

title: Cultural diet frameworks and modern evidence
summary: Multiple traditional dietary frameworks (e.g. Mediterranean, DASH, classical Chinese) share three features supported by modern evidence: moderate evening intake, emphasis on whole foods, and consistent eating windows.

title: Water intake tracking
summary: Consistent hydration tracking improves self-awareness of thirst-related fatigue without changing total daily intake for most adults. Goal: 25–30 mL/kg body weight.
